decision_summary: Proceed with the pre-registered 60/20/20 chronological split. Do NOT rebalance splits, do NOT drop the val fold. Accept that val-fold and test-fold conclusions will be reported with wide bootstrap CIs reflecting the 3-positive minority count per fold.

close_calls_not_triggered.name: late_positives
close_calls_not_triggered.note: Just under trigger but material. Results doc must frame the task as partly detect / partly forecast.

rationale: The pre-registered plan's three-way Phase 2 gate (advance / signal_of_life / null) was explicitly designed to distinguish 'not enough data to conclude' from 'no signal'. With 3 positives per minority fold and bootstrap 95% CIs, most conclusions will land in signal_of_life or null, which is the correct epistemic posture for a 25-positive labeled set.
Rebalancing splits after seeing the halt is a form of test-fold contamination — the plan explicitly forbids post-hoc split-ratio adjustment for the purpose of clearing a gate.

Dropping the val fold to train/test only would break chronological discipline because threshold selection would have to move to train-fold k-fold CV, which conflicts with the plan's 'no k-fold, no shuffling' rule.
Growing the labeled dataset is the correct remedy for a signal_of_life outcome, not a pre-registration change.

label_fixes_applied_during_preflight_aud.reason: Journal lines 50-58 explicitly describe 0DTE LONGs as defending a breached/rolled CCS short strike — hedge_only=True per §N5 of label_rules.md. The proposer-extracted '16:50' was a PT->ET conversion of a 1:50 PM post-hoc recap timestamp, past the 16:00 market close.

data_quality_flags_not_fixed.impact: The positive label is trivially detectable at the 10:00 ET cutoff because the qualifying event is already in the observable window. Classifier task is easy for this row; no label change recommended, but this bias should be noted.
Same as above — detectable at cutoff; no label change recommended.

split_boundaries_frozen.note: These boundaries are frozen by this acknowledgment. Any sensitivity rerun must filter a changed label set to exactly these calendar ranges — indices are NOT recomputed on a different row count.
